resolved_findings.resolution: Resolved: the original finding misread how the canonical_home fields work. In rh_avodah and rh_hodaah, canonical_home has map_root=false and omit_publication_urn=true (review-context-v5.json existing_titles_and_condition_metadata). review-context-v5.json clarifications.canonical_home says this combination means the grouping URN (siddur:rosh_hashanah/musaf/repetition/{avodah,hodaah}_word_parts) is never emitted as a whole-text or publication identity. clarifications.publication_urn says pure word collections leave out a false whole-text identity on purpose. So the URN is an internal grouping/file key, not a canonical home for shared Amidah text. It also makes no claim about Musaf, and it does not contradict omit_publication_urn: it is exactly the URN that the flag suppresses. The real identities are the generic prayer:amidah/... milestones inside, which the paragraphs bind to. validation-source-evidence-v5.json literal_contexts shows the documentary context quoting prayer:amidah/hodaah/{modim,ukhetov,veal_kullam} through explicit seg/@source. bounded-identity-v4.json (approved) found each canonical corresp emitted exactly once per project and none duplicated. The unit identities siddur:rosh_hashanah/minchah_maariv/amidah/{avodah,hodaah} are registered legacy records (siddur.jsonl lines 795 and 798). The titles are unchanged from the accepted metadata (title_unchanged=true). This matches SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME.md 'The same text in several contexts': a siddur: context with milestones carrying the shared prayer: identity.

Resolved as a blocker; kept as nonblocking follow-up NB-F2. urn:x-opensiddur:text:siddur:rosh_hashanah/text/vekhol_hachayyim is an existing registry record with status=canonical (siddur.jsonl line 895, review-context-v5.json existing_registry_records). It is not newly minted. clarifications.legacy_metadata applies the user's instruction to reuse existing identities and not mint replacements, and says migrating legacy names can only be nonblocking follow-up. Binding paragraph 4 to the registered identity is that required reuse. Binding it to an unregistered prayer:amidah/hodaah/vekhol_hachayyim would mint a second identity for the same text against that instruction. Before 1.0 the scheme also says a rename replaces the URN outright (no aliases), which would be a separate, deliberate registry change. bounded-identity-v4.json confirmed this identity is emitted as a milestone corresp exactly once per project, and validation-source-evidence-v5.json shows the documentary context quoting it through seg/@source.

Resolved as a blocker; kept as nonblocking follow-up NB-F3. The main premise of the finding is wrong. clarifications.old_minchah says the Minchah at the start of this festival book is the preparatory weekday Minchah (erev Rosh haShanah), not the festival Amidah. So 'Weekday Minchah' is correct. siddur:rosh_hashanah/... in context_urn names the book's occasion and running order (SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME.md: siddur: names a place in a book's order), not the calendar status of that service. The title is the accepted legacy title, unchanged (old_accepted_title == new_title, title_unchanged=true). The canonical home inherits it as-is, and the clarification marks improving it as separate work. It is header display metadata, not identity or pilot installment text. The identity binding itself is correct: the canonical home is the generic prayer:amidah/hodaah/modim_derabbanan, and the new context siddur:rosh_hashanah/minchah/modim_derabbanan is registered as status=context (bounded-identity-v4.json). The ASCII slug suffix is a real cosmetic defect in both titles, the Hebrew one included, and stays as follow-up.

Resolved. (a) review_encoding: clarifications.review_encoding defines true as a mandatory canonical/encoding review gate that requires a receipt. It is not a pending marker, and completion is recorded in reviews.json, not in this boolean. code-followup-v4.json NB4 (approved) checked that the baseline accepts review_encoding=True only when removing exactly that key reproduces the accepted snapshot (protected_sha256 and every literal_sha256). It also rejects disabling the flag, non-boolean values, and text or title edits. So the flag is the intended gate, not leftover metadata. (b) Empty source_fidelity: clarifications.source_fidelity says that list holds only automatically generated canonical-occurrence comparisons, and literal source quotations are reviewed independently as XML and source blocks. The Numbers 6:24-26 quotation bindings were reviewed and approved in bounded-identity-v4.json: canonical chapter/verse @n, whole verses with no partial-verse over-claim, seg/@source pointing to the canonical bible URN, inner scopes closed before the next content, and the birkat_kohanim intro identity reused across the Shacharit and Musaf placements. This conforms to rule-verse_numbering.md (canonical @n, one milestone per canonical verse). (c) end_reference: true is a segment mapping field (code-followup-v4.json NB4 SEGMENT_MAPPING_FIELDS). It produces the bare same-unit terminator milestone defined in SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME.md 'Ending a scope'. bounded-identity-v4.json observed exactly this: the intro identity closes with a bare prayer-part terminator before the Numbers milestones, and the verse scopes close before the following content. The zikhron canonical home uses end_reference: true the same way on a single bounded word.
evidence: SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME.md 'Ending a scope: the unit-terminating milestone'

resolved_findings.resolution: Explained. rh_avodah is bound through canonical occurrences, so its source_fidelity comparisons are listed automatically. rh_hodaah and amidah_modim_derabbanan are literal documentary contexts (canonical_home.context='literal'; both appear in validation-source-evidence-v5.json literal_contexts with page-break and seg/@source checks). Per clarifications.source_fidelity, an empty list there is expected and does not mean the review is missing. This also explains the 'context' difference noted in N2.

nonblocking_findings.finding: The non-emitted grouping keys siddur:rosh_hashanah/musaf/repetition/{avodah,hodaah}_word_parts carry a misleading Musaf-repetition path for material printed in Minchah/Maariv. They create no identity, but a neutral grouping key would be clearer. The en titles say 'Evening Prayer for the New Year' while the unit URNs say minchah_maariv; these are accepted legacy titles. Optional follow-up only.

Under SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME.md, Vekhol hachayyim is shared Amidah liturgy and would ideally live under prayer:. Migrating the registered siddur:rosh_hashanah/text/vekhol_hachayyim needs a deliberate registry rename decision by the user. It must not be minted as a replacement in this batch.

The accepted legacy title, inherited by canonical_home.title, contains an unrendered ASCII slug ('modim_derabbanan') in both he and en. A separate metadata pass should replace it with proper titles. 'Weekday Minchah' itself is correct.

title.en is in Hebrew (accepted legacy, unchanged). There is no speaker-role metadata, although SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME.md defines role/reader and role/kohanim, and the leader context is implied only by the source URN birkat_kohanim_leshatz. The whitespace-only seg/@source elements between the verses (noted by bounded-identity-v4.json) add noise. Optional follow-up.
Congregational recitation is carried only by a 'description' instruction with no role URN or placement field. Optional role-vocabulary follow-up.

The binding target siddur:rosh_hashanah/musaf/yismechu/text is publication-namespaced for text shared with Shabbat Musaf. This is legacy and covered by the reuse instruction, so any migration is follow-up. The de-Hebr rubric language matches the settled source/XML reviews of the same 'אַם שַׁבָּת.' rubrics. The difference between the record's own condition-instruction hash and the repetition control's is not explained by the evidence here. The original reviewer did not mark it as blocking, and the record matches its own attesting control.

verdict: Approved for the bindings_0 closure scope. None of the four original blockers holds up against the registry and clarification evidence. B1: the Musaf-namespaced URNs are non-emitted grouping keys (map_root=false, omit_publication_urn=true). The real identities are generic prayer:amidah milestones, emitted once each and quoted from the registered legacy minchah_maariv contexts. B2: vekhol_hachayyim reuses an existing registered canonical identity (siddur.jsonl:895), as the user required; renaming it is follow-up. B3: 'Weekday Minchah' correctly names the preparatory erev-Rosh-haShanah Minchah, and the title is unchanged accepted legacy metadata; the slug suffix is cosmetic follow-up. B4: review_encoding=true is a mandatory receipt gate, not a pending flag, and its baseline behaviour is code-verified. The empty source_fidelity list is expected for literal quotations, which the approved identity review covered for Numbers 6:24-26 (canonical numbering, whole verses, closed scopes). end_reference is the scheme's bare scope terminator, and its emitted effect was seen in the XML review. Limits: I did not see reviews.json, so this approval relies on the gate's definition and the code review that it requires a receipt, not on inspecting the receipt. final_sha256 was not recomputed. Code, XML body and export approval stay with their own groups.
